priceSnapshot.note: changePct is -0.43% against OKX open24h of 63,068.4. Against the PRIOR REPORT - today's midday session at 63,165.1 - the move is -367.8 points, -0.58%, over six hours and forty-eight minutes. That is the largest inter-session move this desk has recorded in eleven sessions and it is a DOWN move that erased the entire midday advance and then some. The path is the story. The 21:00Z 1H bar opened 63,065.6, traded to 62,742.9 on 91.4 BTC - roughly three and a half times the volume of the preceding five bars - and settled 62,929.3; the 22:00Z bar extended to 62,715.7 on 89.9 BTC. Inside the single minute 21:40:00-21:41:00Z the OKX perp printed $1,019,573 of liquidations across sixty fills, every one of them long-side. Price has since recovered 81.6 points off the low and is grinding sideways in the 62,750-62,940 band. The run proxy served the spot ticker from a SEVEN-HOUR-STALE cache this session - it returned last 63,150.1 stamped 17:34:20Z - so every OKX number in this report was re-read in-browser from the okx.com origin with a live timestamp inside five minutes of publication.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below $62,715.7 - this session's low, printed on the 22:00Z bar. The line moves DOWN 340.7 points from midday's 63,056.4, and it moves down because midday's line FIRED: the 21:00Z bar settled 62,929.3, a full 127.1 points through it, and the three bars since have all settled below it with no reclaim. That is the cleanest published-exit break of the week and it is the reason this report's stance is REDUCE rather than a continuation of the ADD sequence. What a settled close below 62,715.7 would mean is specific: it would put price under the low of the liquidation flush itself, into the 62,687.9-62,711.1 band where $367,479 of long-side fuel already burned between 21:40Z and 22:41Z, and it would open the 5-day low at 62,521.8 with nothing measured in between.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $63,090.5 - the 1H ema50, which is also within 43 points of the 1H ema20 at 63,048.0 and therefore reclaims the whole near stack in one move. The gate drops 299.5 points from midday's 63,390.0 because the level that produced that gate is now 293 points overhead and, more importantly, because the structure has changed underneath it: price spent this session losing every EMA on every timeframe, so the question is no longer whether it can extend a breakout but whether it can get back inside the box it just left. Requiring the 1H ema50 rather than the session high keeps the rule this desk adopted on 16 August morning - anchor the gate where price actually trades - and applies it to a downside regime for the first time. The confirmation that would matter beyond the price itself is open interest FALLING through the reclaim, which would say the new shorts are covering rather than that longs are being tempted back in.

decisionBox.changed: Everything moved down and the stance inverted. The position goes from ADD to REDUCE, the first REDUCE this desk has published since 14 August endday, because the midday reduce line was broken on a settled bar and never reclaimed. The reduce line falls 340.7 points to 62,715.7; the add gate falls 299.5 points to 63,090.5; invalidation falls 442.5 points from 62,964.3 to 62,521.8, the lowest low of the last thirty 4H bars and the first level below the flush with any structural claim. The stopOrder flag flips to RECOMMENDED for the first time in four sessions at $62,680.0 - 117.3 points under spot and 35.7 points under the bottom of the burned cluster - because this is the last report before a six-and-a-half-hour unattended gap and price is sitting 81.6 points above a level that has already proven it can take a million dollars of longs out in sixty seconds.

overnightRisk: Three specific things make the next six and a half hours the highest-risk window this desk has framed in two weeks. FIRST, positioning got MORE crowded into the flush, not less. Open interest is $2,122,316,880 against $2,115,031,058 at midday - UP $7,285,822, +0.34% - while price fell 367.8 points, and the OKX long/short account ratio rose to 2.24 from 2.22. Rising open interest into a decline is new positions being opened, and a rising account ratio into a decline is retail buying it. Both readings say the long side was rebuilt at a worse price immediately after $1,645,794 of longs were force-closed, so the fuel that burned tonight has already been partly replaced. SECOND, the liquidation band price is currently sitting IN - 62,763.2 to 62,784.5, $164,056 all long-side - was still taking fills as recently as 00:33:22Z, three minutes before the last read. That is not a spent cluster; it is an active one, and spot at 62,797.3 is thirteen points above its top edge. THIRD, the ETF creation channel reopens in roughly thirteen and a half hours with its last three published rows negative - 12 August -$61.1m, 13 August -$131.1m, 14 August -$56.2m, -$248.4m across the streak - so the largest structural buyer has been a net seller every time it has been open this week, and Sunday-night thin liquidity has to carry the tape until it returns. The concrete overnight scenario to plan for is a settled break of 62,715.7 running the 62,687.9-62,711.1 band and then finding no measured support until 62,521.8, a 194-point air pocket. The 1H ATR at 120.43 says that is roughly a 1.6-bar move - entirely ordinary. This is why the stop at $62,680.0 is flagged rather than merely mentioned: a resting order is the only protection that works while nobody is watching, and it is placed 35.7 points below the burned cluster so a wick into the fuel does not take it out. The bull case for the gap is thin but real: the flush was violent and one-sided, funding is only +0.01% so the carry is not punitive, and price has already put 81.6 points between itself and the low without any new bid arriving.

An active long-liquidation band directly beneath the mark is the single most immediate risk on this board; it means leveraged longs are still being closed out at this price, not that they were closed out an hour ago.

$624,798 across just THREE fills at 62,921.5 exactly, 100% LONG-side, inside two seconds at 21:40:04-21:40:05Z. This is the largest single cluster the desk has ever recorded on this feed and it is 34% of the entire 24h liquidation total in two seconds. It is also completely SPENT - it detonated on the way down and price is now 124.2 points below it. Reading it as overhead resistance is wrong; reading it as the receipt for the cascade that defined this session is right, and its size is the measure of how leveraged the long side was at 62,921.

calibration.note: The prior report is today's 2026-08-16-midday, published at 12:55:00-05:00 with spot at 63,165.1. Its reduce line at 63,056.4 FIRED and fired decisively: the 21:00Z 1H bar settled 62,929.3, 127.1 points through it, and the 22:00Z and 23:00Z bars settled 62,917.2 and 62,903.9 with no reclaim on any settled bar. Its add gate at 63,390.0 was never approached - the window high was 63,233.4, short by 156.6 points. actingHelped is FALSE and the size of the miss matters. Midday bought a fifth 12 USDT spot tranche at 63,165.1 and spot marks 367.8 points lower at 62,797.3, -0.58%, roughly -0.070 USDT on that tranche - more than double the largest miss in the file and the end of four consecutive sessions of sub-three-cent errors. Two things are worth recording precisely. FIRST, the placement discipline that had been keeping misses tiny failed here for a structural reason: midday bought 108.7 points above its own reduce line and 132.1 points above the 63,033 cluster it had itself identified as the only unburned fuel on the map, which had been sufficient buffer on every prior session; tonight price went 449.4 points through the entry and the buffer was irrelevant because the move was a cascade, not a drift. Placement protects against drift and does nothing against a cascade - that is a genuinely new lesson from this file. SECOND, and to midday's credit, the report named the exact mechanism of its own failure in its own addIf text: it wrote that the break which fired the gate ran on FALLING open interest, that this is the signature of shorts covering rather than longs building, and that the move needed a real buyer to appear. No buyer appeared. The observation was correct and the weighting was wrong - the report reduced tranche size from 15 to 12 on that concern rather than declining the trade. This is the second time in three sessions that a report has correctly identified the argument against its own action and then acted anyway at reduced size, which suggests the desk's failure mode has migrated from bad observation to insufficient conviction in its own caveats.
